description: PolyGNN is Python software for three-dimensional building reconstruction from point clouds using a polyhedron-based graph neural network. Its native repository describes this building-reconstruction purpose and labels the implementation with its ISPRS 2024 work. The TUM2TWIN airborne-laser-scan description links PolyGNN to a synthetic Munich building benchmark generated with HELIOS++ and LoD2 city models. This source-established role makes the software a preparation tool for built-environment geometry used in digital city models. It is catalogued separately from the already represented PolyGNN Munich Data benchmark, which is related input and evaluation data. Geographic coverage depends on the supplied building observations; the linked benchmark is Munich, and wider geographic validation is not established. The public repository is available under the MIT licence and identifies Python as its main language. Cost is free for the published open-source implementation. The inspected metadata does not establish a command-line interface, package API, supported deployment, internal point/mesh formats or computational requirements. A limitation is that code, README, model weights and article bodies were not inspected, and no reconstruction was run or independently evaluated. The repository metadata reports a push on 13 March 2025; that date does not establish ongoing maintenance or scientific validation.
